scores.answer:
Qualcomm guided fiscal Q3 2026 GAAP diluted EPS to $1.26–$1.46 [1]. Reported GAAP diluted EPS for the quarter was $1.87 [2], which is $0.41 above the top of the range [1][2]. The guidance excluded provisions for proposed tax law changes, future asset impairments and pending legal matters, other than probable and estimable future legal amounts [1].

scores.question: How did Nvidia's revenue change over the last four quarters, from fiscal Q3 2026 to fiscal Q2 2027?
failure_details: 0 numbers_cited: a sentence with a number has no citation: Nvidia's revenue rose in each of the three sequential steps from fiscal Q3 2026 to fiscal Q2 2027, and rose 68.79% overall across the period.
scores.answer:
Nvidia's revenue rose in each of the three sequential steps from fiscal Q3 2026 to fiscal Q2 2027 [1][2][3][4]. Overall, revenue grew 68.79% over that span [1][4].
- **FY2026Q3:** Revenue was $57,006M [1].
- **FY2026Q4:** Revenue was $68,127M, up 19.51% from the prior quarter [1][2].
- **FY2027Q1:** Revenue was $81,615M, up 19.80% from the prior quarter [2][3].
- **FY2027Q2:** Revenue was $96,221M, up 17.90% from the prior quarter [3][4].
The FY2026Q4 figure is derived from the annual 10-K total less the nine-month year-to-date figure, not a directly reported quarterly number [2]. The other three quarters are stored values as reported in their filings [1][3][4].

scores.question: What is the trend in Meta's capex over the last four quarters, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026?
scores.answer:
Meta's capex rose over the four quarters from Q3 2025 to Q2 2026, with one dip in Q1 2026. Quarterly capex was $18,829M in Q3 2025 [1], $21,383M in Q4 2025 [2], $18,997M in Q1 2026 [3], and $30,116M in Q2 2026 [4].
- Q3 to Q4 2025: up 13.56% [1][2].
- Q4 2025 to Q1 2026: down 11.16% [2][3].
- Q1 to Q2 2026: up 58.53% [3][4].
- Overall, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026: up 59.94% [1][4].
- Highest minus lowest quarter (Q2 2026 less Q3 2025): $11,287M [1][4].
The Q1 2026 dip was the only decline in the window, and Q2 2026 was the largest quarter by a wide margin.

Sources:
[1] META 10-Q filed 2025-10-30: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828025047240/meta-20250930.htm

scores.question: According to Nvidia's 10-Q MD&A for fiscal Q2 2027, what drove the growth in Data Center revenue?
failure_details: 0 numbers_grounded: '$89,023 million' is in no evidence: Data Center revenue was $89,023 million in the quarter, versus $41,096 million a year earlier [E4].
0 numbers_grounded: '$41,096 million' is in no evidence: Data Center revenue was $89,023 million in the quarter, versus $41,096 million a year earlier [E4].
scores.answer:
Nvidia's fiscal Q2 2027 10-Q MD&A attributes the Data Center revenue growth to the ramp of its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. Data Center revenue was up 117% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially, "driven by the ramp of our Blackwell Ultra infrastructure" [1].
- Hyperscale revenue more than doubled year over year and rose 13% sequentially, on the strength of Blackwell Ultra [1].
- ACIE revenue rose 138% year over year and 25% sequentially, driven by end-demand from AI natives, enterprises, and sovereign customers, as well as hyperscalers utilizing AI clouds [1].

scores.question: What does Tesla's 10-K say in its risk factors about depending on Elon Musk?
scores.answer:
Tesla's risk factors say the company is "highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer" [1][2]. They note that Musk "does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla," because he also holds positions at other companies, and that he is "highly active in our management" [1][2]. A related risk factor on key employees repeats the dependence and adds that none of Tesla's key employees has an employment agreement for a specific term [3][4].
The most recent 10-K I could retrieve is for FY2025 [5], but the passage returned from it was on a different topic, so I could not confirm the current wording there. The quotes above come from the FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks.

[1] TSLA 10-K FY2023Q4, ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS, characters 89357-91730: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/tsla-20231231.htm
